user_message:
Speech context: Greta Thunberg, Address to the COP24 plenary, COP24, Katowice, Poland, 2018-12-12.

Annotate every numbered sentence below. Return one entry per sentence, using the number in brackets as seg_id.

[2] My name is Greta Thunberg.
[3] I am 15 years old and I'm from Sweden.
[4] I speak on behalf of climate justice now.
[5] Many people say that Sweden is just a small country and it doesn't matter what we do.
[6] But I've learned that you are never too small to make a difference.
[7] And if a few children can get headlines all over the world just by not going to school, then imagine what we could all do together if we really wanted to.
[8] But to do that, we have to speak clearly, no matter how uncomfortable that may be.
[9] You only speak of green, eternal economic growth because you are too scared of being unpopular.
[10] You only talk about moving forward
[11] with the same bad ideas that got us into this mess, even when the only sensible thing to do is pull the emergency brake.
[12] You are not mature enough to tell it like it is.
[13] Even that burden you leave to us children.
[14] But I don't care about being popular.
[15] I care about climate justice and a living planet.
[16] Our civilization is being sacrificed for the opportunity of a very small number of people to continue making enormous amounts of money.
[17] Our biosphere is being sacrificed so that rich people in countries like mine can live in luxury.
[18] It is the sufferings of the many which pay for the luxuries of the few.
[19] The year 2078
[20] I will celebrate my 75th birthday.
[21] If I have children, maybe they will spend that day with me.
[22] Maybe they will ask me about you.
[23] Maybe they will ask why you didn't do anything while there still was time to act.
[24] You say you love your children above all else, and yet you're stealing their future in front of their very eyes.
[25] Until you start focusing on what needs to be done, rather than what is politically possible, there is no hope.
[26] We cannot solve a crisis without treating it as a crisis.
[27] We need to keep the fossil fuels in the ground and we need to focus on equity.
[28] And if solutions within this system are so impossible to find, then maybe we should change the system itself.
[29] We have not come here to beg world leaders to care.
[30] You have ignored us in the past and you will ignore us again.
[31] We have run out of excuses and we are running out of time.
[32] We have come here to let you know that change is coming, whether you like it or not.
[33] The real power belongs to the people.
[34] Thank you.
[35] you
